Response deck

Hollow Oak Cider: Hollow Oak Still

Opening1
Objective

What has to change, by how much and by when

  • Attitudinal: shift the lead drinker from 'cider is not for me' to 'a still orchard cider is worth trying', and build awareness of Still among them.
  • The 55+ rural core must not be alienated.
  • shift the lead drinker from 'cider is not for me' to 'a still orchard cider is worth trying', and build awareness of Still among them. Making Hollow Oak cool with Gen Z is secondary, and the 55+ rural core must not be alienated.
Sources [1] [2] (appendix)2
The real question

Lead drinkers like the idea of an honest apple drink, so Still has to arrive without the baggage the word cider carries.

Lead drinkers like the idea of an honest apple drink; the word cider gets in the way.

Background
Still launches in September; summer work builds anticipation, not sales. GB crafted cider value is up 7.6% while retail volume is down 1.7%.
Sources [1] (appendix)3
The real question

Lead drinkers say cider has come to mean fizzy, sweet and heavy, so they order something else.

  • Lead drinkers say cider means fizzy, sweet and heavy, so order something else.
  • Lead with what is absent, not heritage.
Sources [1] (appendix)4
Insight

People who like the idea of an honest apple drink say cider has come to mean fizzy, sweet and heavy, so they order something else.

Lead drinkers like the idea of an honest apple drink, but fizzy is their first word against cider. Still should lead with 'no fizz' as the reason to try it.

Our insight.

Lead drinker line: 'I like the idea of an honest apple drink, but cider has come to mean fizzy, sweet and heavy.' To confirm.

Lead drinkers rarely drink cider.

Among ciders, Magners owns fizz and serving over ice.

Sources [1] (appendix)5
Insight

We are talking to drinkers who already like apples but not cider, and the core who love the bottle must still feel at home.

Drinkers aged 25-40 who rarely drink cider, women slightly ahead.

Who the work is written for

Nell. Brings one good bottle to a Friday supper, never the cider, and has never been given a reason to.

The 55+ rural core is protected, not targeted. Gen Z appeal is secondary, not the lead.

Sources [1] (appendix)6
Proposition

Hollow Oak Still gives you the whole orchard in every glass, with nothing fizzy or heavy in the way.

From

Cider is not for me.

To

A still orchard cider is worth trying.

Why they will believe it

  • Orchard-grown: fruit from the brand's own orchards.
  • 140 years of growing apples.
  • The client must supply how Still keeps depth of flavour without fizz.

The objection it must beat: a no-fizz cider risks telling the 55+ core their bottle was the problem. Still is an addition, not a correction. We never criticise the current bottle. Sales growth counts all products.

Sources [1] (appendix)7
Competition

What else the client could choose, and why this wins

The alternativeWhy you might pick itHow we win
One of the other two routes in the three-route presentationThe client asked for three routes and may prefer a different territory.This is the only route where the drinker's complaint and Still's product difference are the same word, so the insight becomes the proposition.
Show that one word, fizz, links the drinker's objection, the product and the trial we can measure.
Sources [1] [2] (appendix)8
Territories

Territory: Minus the Fizz

Make the missing fizz the whole message: Still is cider without the one thing lead drinkers hold against it.

Why it fits
Lead drinkers turn cider down for its fizz (brief:insight). Still removes that complaint and leads with absence, not heritage.
Mood
Spare and confident: white space, one bottle, one line. Bubbles shown by their absence. A soft pour, no hiss.

Cider, minus the fizz.

Illustrative, not final
9
Territories

Territory: The Order

Win the few seconds at a friend's table, the pub or a Friday supper when cider gets ruled out.

Why it fits
Cider loses at the order, before anyone tastes it; these drinkers choose quickly, in front of others (brief:audience).
Mood
Warm, observed, slightly comic: hands round shared tables, bars, the half-second hesitation before ordering. Natural light, no famous faces.

The cider for people who don't order cider.

Illustrative, not final
10
Territories

Territory: Poured Slow

Leave the race for fizzy, ice-cold refreshment to everyone else and make Still the unhurried, orchard-tasting pour.

Why it fits
Rivals sell cider on fizz and ice (brief:competitor_context). Still takes the open still position, with 'Orchard-grown' as taste, not heritage.
Mood
Slow, tactile, sensory: long takes of a calm pour, light through the glass. Natural palette, no ice, frost or condensation.

No hiss, no rush. Orchard-grown, poured still.

Illustrative, not final
11
The idea

Hollow Oak Still names the one thing it leaves out, so the missing fizz stops being a gap and becomes the reason to try it.

12
The work

Key visual

Role: Carries the whole idea in one picture: one can, one glass and a still surface, with an empty space where the bubbles would be.

Hollow Oak Still. From September.

Dramatises the rejection half of the insight ('turn cider down for its fizz'). It shows the fizz gone and makes the missing fizz the reason to try it. The absence is shown, not a taste or health benefit, so no claim is made (req:R41).
13
The work

Out of home

Role: In summer it builds anticipation near the pubs, shops and supper routes of lead drinkers. From September it turns that curiosity into looking for Still on shelf. Sizes: UK 96 sheet, UK 48 sheet, UK 6 sheet, UK adshel 6 sheet and UK D6.

The honest apple drink you had in mind. Minus the fizz.

One good cider for the table. Minus the fizz.

Coming in September.

Hollow Oak Still. Look for it from September.

Dramatises the wanting half of the insight ('like the idea of an honest apple drink'). The drinker's own picture of the drink is the headline, and the missing fizz is the only thing added.

The work

Storyboard frames

Role: Four stills, read in order, set the idea at the shared moment of ordering: a Friday supper, where cider is ruled out before anyone tastes it.

Dramatises both halves in sequence. Frames 1 and 2 show the rejection half, where cider is turned down at the table. Frames 3 and 4 answer with the wanting half, an honest apple drink with nothing fizzy in the way. The frames move the drinker from 'Cider is not for me' to 'A still orchard cider is worth trying'.

The work

Packshot

Role: Shows the new recyclable can clearly, so lead drinkers know exactly what to look for from September. It carries the reasons to believe in plain, exact facts.

Hollow Oak Still

The whole orchard in every glass. Nothing fizzy in the way.

Orchard-grown, from our own orchards.

Dramatises the wanting half ('an honest apple drink'). Orchard-grown fruit and a still pour make the honest drink concrete. The packshot claims only what the brief supplies and leaves the method line open until Hollow Oak supplies it.

Each channel has one job

ChannelIts one job

How it runs

How the plan works harder than its media list

  • The headline is the drinker's own complaint turned round: we remove the word they use against cider.
  • It reads like a farmers' market board, not an ad, and stands apart from the ice-and-fizz and pastoral cider codes.

Measurement

We will measure awareness of Still and trial among lead drinkers, and whether the core keeps buying the bottle.

What we measureBaselineHow
Awareness of Still among 25-40 drinkers who rarely drink ciderNone: set before launchSurvey before summer, after summer and after launch.
Lead drinkers agreeing 'a still orchard cider is worth trying'None: set before launchAsk the from-to statement in the same survey.
Trial of Still among lead drinkersNone: set before launchAsk in the post-launch survey.
Current bottle sales, 55+ coreNone: set before launchCompare with the same period before launch, using client sales data.
Total Hollow Oak sales growth, all productsNone: set before launchCompare with the prior year over 12 months from launch, for the client to confirm.

What the work must always carry, and never do

  • Legal: include a responsible drinking line.
  • Legal: no reduced-sugar, health or mood claims (CAP/BCAP).
  • Sugar story held until R&D confirms.
  • Legal: any competition needs legal terms and a no-purchase route.
  • why legal wants no apples in visuals; show none.
  • Brand assets: logo, orchard, new recyclable can.
  • whether the old bottle sits beside the can.

Dry, warm, irreverent wit with serious craft behind it.

    Territories

    We recommend 'Minus the Fizz'

    TerritoryWhy (or why not)
    Minus the FizzIt makes the drinker's objection and the product difference the same word, so it is the insight turned straight into the proposition, with a clear, simple hook that runs across every channel, though 'no fizz' needs distinctive identity work to be ownable.
    Poured SlowIt uses the open still position against rivals who own fizz and ice, and gives a distinctive calm tone, but it risks drifting into orchard-heritage cliché or turning sleepy, and it is one step removed from the drinker's own complaint.
    The OrderIt correctly spots the quick, social choice moment, but it rests on thin ordering-behaviour evidence, is tied to distribution that is not confirmed, and carries the most category-safety risk by centring on shared drinking occasions.

    How it runs

    How we would run it with you

    1

    Test the insight and the line 'Cider, minus the fizz' with 25-40 drinkers who rarely drink cider, and with the 55+ core, before finalising.

    2

    Hollow Oak supplies how Still is made without fizz and the responsible drinking wording. Legal explains the no-apples rule and whether the old bottle sits beside the can.

    3

    Confirm whether '140 years of growing apples' counts as heritage held for other assets. If it does, drop it from the packshot.

    4

    Present the routes by Friday and take the chosen one to the board by month end.

    5

    Once the budget is known after Q1, choose which out-of-home sizes run and where, starting from the key visual and packshot.

    6

    Run the summer anticipation copy. Switch to 'Look for it from September' at launch and measure against the agreed baselines.

    27
    Appendix

    Questions we would settle in the first fortnight

    • What is the production budget figure, does it include VAT, and does media sit inside it? — Answer: Production budget is £120,000 all-in, excluding VAT, and media sits outside it. Spend it on the 15-second film, stills and in-store; no TV or stunt.
    • What is the baseline and period for the 30% sales uplift, and does it include Still? — Answer: Baseline is last year's total Hollow Oak sales volume; target is plus 30 percent over 12 months from the September launch, across all products including Still.
    • Can legal explain the 'no apples' concern? — Answer: Legal worry is apple imagery implying a fruit or health claim we cannot back. Hard rule: no apples anywhere in visuals. Show the oak, bare orchard trees, the can, the glass.
    • How is Still made without fizz, and what does that do to the taste? — Answer: Still is made like the sparkling cider but left uncarbonated, which gives a rounder, softer, drier taste. Say that plainly, with no reduced-sugar claim.
    • Do you accept one lead audience (25-40 rare cider drinkers) and one lead line, rather than all four 'Still' lines? — Answer: Yes. One lead audience, 25-40 drinkers who rarely drink cider, and one lead line only: Still. Hollow Oak.
    • What is the competition mechanic, and will legal supply the terms and a no-purchase route? — Answer: Win a weekend in the orchards. Entry on social, after launch, with a no-purchase route. Legal terms come from the client's legal team before anything is published.
    • Must the old bottle appear beside the can? — Answer: Yes. Show the new can as the hero and the old bottle once, small, beside it, so core drinkers recognise the brand.
    • Which measures count as success, and is there budget for a tracker or holdout? — Answer: Primary: trial of Still among 25-40s, read through sales and distribution after September. Secondary: awareness in a before-and-after tracker. An award is a bonus.
